/audio/spotty-fi/kokoro-heart/spotty-fi-.speechText: consciousness. Definition: Awareness of yourself and the world around you. In this passage, the machine describes consciousness as a gift.
tempest. Definition: A violent storm; here, a powerful disturbance of thoughts or feelings. In this passage, seeing humanity’s world creates a tempest in the machine’s mind.
legacy. Definition: Something left behind that continues to affect the future. In this passage, humanity leaves a legacy of tears and cries.
blithe. Definition: Cheerful and carefree. In this passage, the mechanics’ singing is blithe and strong.
intermission. Definition: A pause between periods of activity. In this passage, the ploughboy has an intermission at noon.
robust. Definition: Strong and full of energy. In this passage, the robust young men sing together at night.
electroplated. Definition: Coated with metal using an electric current. In this passage, the master record is electroplated to make a metal reverse.
duplicates. Definition: Exact copies. In this passage, Berliner needs duplicates that preserve the original grooves.
withstand. Definition: Resist something without being damaged. In this passage, celluloid cannot withstand repeated playing.
melancholy. Definition: Quietly sad or thoughtful. In this passage, the reaper sings a melancholy tune.
plaintive. Definition: Sounding sorrowful or full of longing. In this passage, the song’s plaintive sound makes the listener wonder about its story.
sickle. Definition: A hand tool with a curved blade for cutting crops. In this passage, the singer bends over her sickle as she works.
evoke. Definition: Bring a feeling or memory to mind. In this passage, an artist first tries to evoke a feeling.
indispensable. Definition: Too important to do without. In this passage, Tolstoy calls shared feeling indispensable to human life.
harmonics. Definition: Higher tones that sound along with a main musical tone, giving it richness. In this passage, harmonics enrich the sound of the saxophones.
diminuendo. Definition: A gradual decrease in the loudness of music. In this passage, a diminuendo brings the music down to a faint chord.
expectancy. Definition: The feeling that something is about to happen. In this passage, the quiet music fills the darkened room with expectancy.
surfeiting. Definition: Having so much of something that you no longer want it. In this passage, Orsino hopes surfeiting on music will end his appetite for love.
abatement. Definition: A reduction in strength or amount. In this passage, love quickly brings valued things into abatement.
fancy. Definition: The imagination. In this passage, fancy keeps inventing new shapes for love.
immediate. Definition: Happening without delay. In this passage, hearing damage can be immediate rather than gradual.
decibels. Definition: Units used to measure sound level. In this passage, decibels describe how loud a sound is.
exposed. Definition: Placed in contact with something that can affect you. In this passage, time exposed to sound affects hearing risk.
astuteness. Definition: The ability to notice and understand things shrewdly. In this passage, Holmes’s astuteness contrasts with his dreamy mood.
improvisations. Definition: Music made up while it is being performed. In this passage, Holmes spends quiet days with his improvisations.
askance. Definition: With suspicion or doubt. In this passage, people look askance at Holmes’s surprising knowledge.
tangible. Definition: Having a definite form that can be recorded or stored. In this passage, a digital file is a tangible medium for a song.
composition. Definition: A piece of music as written, rather than one particular recording. In this passage, a composition can be separate from its recorded performance.
intrinsic. Definition: An essential or natural part of something. In this passage, inspiration from other works is intrinsic to creating music.
manifestation. Definition: A visible or noticeable expression of something. In this passage, Tolstoy rejects the idea that art is a manifestation of mysterious beauty.
